newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Explosion halts Grand Petrochem plant.
newsitem.headline: Explosion halts Grand Petrochem plant.

text.p: Taiwan's Grand Petrochemical said on Monday an explosion late on Sunday at its Kaohsiung plant had halted production but no injury reported.
"The explosion did not cause any injury, because not many workers worked on Sunday," a company official told Reuters.
The official said the explosion blew the top of all six of Grand Petrochemical's acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene (ABS) powder storage tankers away.
The cause of the explosion has yet to be determined, but the official said it was likely to be static electricity that caused a spark at the storage tankers.
Local media reported that the explosion would cost Grand Petrochemical over T$200 million (US$7.16 million).
Grand Petrochem produces two main products -- ABS and styrene monomer (SM). It can turn out 200 tonnes of ABS and 50 tonnes of SM per day, local media said.
ABS is used in making cases for computer monitors and other electrical appliances.
